note: Track hearing-changes, mix step 4: the 1st, 4th, 5th and 6th chords mixed, counted the long way once as chord tokens, followed in a new order, then with chords held for two bars, then in a new key. The key is moves (any key): the old Key selector is gone, and the last section's line says what stays the same in the new key. Missing: backing-track cannot hide its chord boxes (the text asks the player to look away) and plays a fixed order, not a new one each round.

exercise.title: 1, 4, 5 and 6 in any order
exercise.why: Each chord of a key keeps its own distance from home, so the 4th, 5th and 6th chords sound the same in any order and in any key once you hear them against the 1st chord.

cells.text:
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of {{=key}} major, built on {{1}}. {{chord:IV}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}, {{chord:V}} the 5th chord, built on {{5}}, and {{chord:vi}} the 6th chord, built on {{6}}.
Press Play below to start the backing track: the four chords in a new order. Look away from the chord boxes and say each chord's number as it arrives, 1, 4, 5 or 6, then look at the lit box to check.
If you lose your place, wait for the 1st chord and count on from there.

Press Play below to start the backing track: a longer round, and some chords stay for two bars, so you can't count your way to the next change. Look away and say the number only when you hear the chord move, then look to check.
Practice until you can name a chord before its bar is over.

Press Play below to start the backing track in a new key. Listen to the first chord, the 1st chord, then look away and say the numbers.
Practice until the number comes as each chord starts.
In the new key the chords have other names, and each number sits at the same distance from home.
